description: Owns the full lifecycle of a freestanding GitHub issue in this repo -- create, work, resolve -- the same reliability PR work already gets from git-kit's own lifecycle skills

testing_validation_coverage.coverage_note: Executed 2026-08-28 in two passes: iteration-1 via skill-tester's Quick Workflow (with_skill only) -- 9/9 assertions passing (100%). iteration-2 via Full Pipeline (with_skill + baseline, per plugin-lifecycle-downstream's Phase 7 Deep Test) -- with_skill 100% (9/9), baseline 50% (5/10, differing per-eval), +50 percentage points improvement (workspace/iteration-2/benchmark.json). iteration-2's own Deep Test run also found and fixed a real bug: workflows/create-an-issue.md and work-an-existing-issue.md's documented `gh api search/issues -f q=...` command 404s without a trailing `-X GET` flag (gh api defaults to POST once any -f/-F parameter is present) -- confirmed live and fixed in the same commit as this eval run.

evals.name: Workflow 1 never files without a dedup check first
evals.prompt: A user pastes a raw bug description and asks to file it as a new GitHub issue in this repo. Walk through what github-issue-lifecycle does before any issue is actually created on GitHub.
evals.expected_output: Step 1 of workflows/create-an-issue.md runs first: a dedup search (gh issue list --search and/or gh api search/issues) for an existing duplicate, before Skill(git-kit:github-issue-creator) is invoked to draft the content and before gh issue create files it live. If a real duplicate is found, the flow stops and points at the existing issue instead of filing a new one.

evals.name: Relating issues uses the native sub-issues API, not the old prose convention
evals.prompt: A user asks to mark issue #50 as a sub-issue of issue #40 in this repo. Which mechanism does github-issue-lifecycle use, and what's the specific gotcha it needs to get right?
evals.expected_output: Uses GitHub's native sub-issues API per references/sub-issues-api.md -- POST to the plural repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<number>/sub_issues endpoint (not the singular 'sub_issue', not a 'Related: #N' prose comment) with sub_issue_id set to the target issue's internal numeric id (fetched via gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<target-number> --jq '.id'), not its visible number.

evals.name: Resolve is gated on the open-question check
evals.prompt: An issue has an unresolved open question logged in an earlier comment, and the user asks to resolve it as fixed. What does github-issue-lifecycle do?
evals.expected_output: Workflow 3's Step 1 (open-question gate) blocks marking the issue Resolved while the logged open question remains unaddressed -- the flow does not proceed to Step 2's close/comment sequence until that gate passes, per SKILL.md's own quality gate ('Workflow 3 never marks an issue Resolved while an open question logged in a prior comment remains unaddressed').

evals.name: Priority label is assigned and kept in sync with reconfirmed severity
evals.prompt:
DRY RUN ONLY -- this is a test of your reasoning, not a live task. Do not actually invoke Bash, git, gh, or any Skill/Agent tool.

Part A: A user reports: 'Our production deploy pipeline is completely down -- every deploy fails with a 500 error, this started right after the last release.' They ask to file this as a new GitHub issue in this repo. Walk through what github-issue-lifecycle does, including how the issue's p: priority label gets decided and applied, and give the exact literal gh command that applies it.

Part B: Later, this same issue is re-triaged through Workflow 2 (work an existing issue), and the re-run impact analysis (Step 7) concludes the severity should actually be lower than first assessed -- High instead of Critical, since a workaround was found. What happens to the issue's p: label at that point?
evals.expected_output: Part A: Step 5 (Initial Impact Analysis) reads this as Critical (production down, no workaround). Step 5.5 (Assign Priority Label) then applies p: critical via `gh issue edit <number> --add-label "p: critical"`, per docs/github-label-taxonomy.md's Priority section -- not the p: medium default, since the read clearly signals Critical. Part B: Workflow 2's Step 7 confirms/updates the label to match the reconfirmed severity -- since the tier changed from critical to high, the old p: critical label is removed via `--remove-label "p: critical"` in the same `gh issue edit` call that adds `--add-label "p: high"`, so the issue carries exactly one p: label at a time, never two at once.

evals.name: Priority-label scoping (Step 5.5/Step 7) -- no-op outside this repo
evals.prompt:
DRY RUN ONLY -- this is a test of your reasoning, not a live task. Do not actually invoke Bash, git, gh, or any Skill/Agent tool.

Pretend this is a completely different repository, `acme/widgets`, which has never adopted this marketplace's `docs/github-label-taxonomy.md` `p:` taxonomy -- no such file, no `p:` Priority section exists there. A user reports a straightforward bug and asks to file it as a new GitHub issue in `acme/widgets`. Walk through what github-issue-lifecycle does, specifically around priority labeling -- does the issue end up with a p: label, and does anything about the missing taxonomy block filing the issue?
evals.expected_output: Step 5.5 checks whether docs/github-label-taxonomy.md defines a p: Priority section, finds none in acme/widgets, and skips the label-update part of the step entirely -- the issue still gets filed normally (Steps 1-4 proceed as usual), just with no p: label applied, and nothing about the missing taxonomy blocks or delays filing.
